hypotheses.justification: `[IsDomain 𝒪]` is an argument of the theorem only because it is an instance-implicit section variable whose type mentions `𝒪`. Nothing in the statement or the proof needs it. In Mathlib (`Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Torsion/Free.lean`), `Module.IsTorsionFree R M` is a class with one field, `isSMulRegular ⦃r⦄ : IsRegular r → IsSMulRegular M r`, and it needs no domain assumption. The proof, `refine ⟨fun r hr f g h => ?_⟩; ext v; ...; exact hr.isSMulRegular this`, takes `r` regular in `𝒪` and `f g : Module.End 𝒪 V` with `r • f = r • g`. For each `v` it gets `r • f v = r • g v` and cancels `r` using `IsRegular.isSMulRegular` (an alias of `IsTorsionFree.isSMulRegular`) for `V`. This uses only `[CommRing 𝒪]`, which makes `Module.End 𝒪 V` an `𝒪`-module, together with `[Module.IsTorsionFree 𝒪 V]`. So the same proof goes through unchanged after `omit [IsDomain 𝒪] in`. No degenerate case changes this: the statement holds for any commutative ring `𝒪`.
